_comment: Timing of the selected Quarter-Rate 4:1 MUX Structures slide (ISSCC 2019 paper 6.7, slide 7). This is a circuit-derived illustrative timing example, not a reproduction of measured timing.
Each UI is one output symbol. 14-GHz clocks have period 4 UI; 7-GHz clocks have period 8 UI. 90 degrees at 14 GHz and 45 degrees at 7 GHz both equal 1 UI.

Explicit common phase convention (not specified by the slide): CK0,14G rises at t=0; CK0,7G rises at t=-1 UI. Other 14-GHz and 7-GHz phases are delayed by i UI. Divider complementary phases are implicit.

An illustrative 0.25-UI 8:4-MUX propagation delay places R0=a at -0.75 UI. Latch propagation delay is also 0.25 UI. These are visualization choices, not reported device delays. Setup/hold, skew and nonoverlap must be budgeted in implementation.

Each latch is modeled as level-sensitive: when transparent its output follows its input after the propagation delay, and when opaque it holds. A bubble means LOW-transparent; no bubble means HIGH-transparent.

The 1-UI pulse convention is CK1=C0&C90, CK2=C90&C180, CK3=C180&C270, CK4=C270&C0. For lane i=0..3 its window is [i+1+4k, i+2+4k) UI. Thus selection occupies the latter half of the corresponding high-transparent interval.

Both structures output a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h,i,j,k,l over t=1..13 UI. Q/L lane i becomes a+i at i+0.25 UI. All selected data was checked stable throughout each 1-UI pulse. Hatched regions omit preceding words.
Colors identify data lanes: R0 yellow, R1 orange, R2 blue, R3 green. Input-pair assignment to the 2:1 muxes is chosen to give the shown serial order.
WaveDrom 3.7.0, narrow skin. One wave character is 0.25 UI. Zero-width-space tick tokens leave minor ticks unlabeled.

All four R inputs change simultaneously at -0.75+4k UI. For each lane, master Mi tracks while its CK14 is low, and slave Qi tracks while CK14 is high. The pair behaves as a rising-edge register; all eight physical latch outputs are plotted.
First tracked-word transitions: M0/M1 at -0.5 UI, M2 at 0.25 UI, M3 at 1.25 UI; Q0/Q1/Q2/Q3 at 0.25/1.25/2.25/3.25 UI. Subsequent words repeat every 4 UI.
The lane-0 mode band names the transparent latch (M0/Q0 or L0); hold means the single latch is opaque. Other lanes have the same mode shifted by i UI.
Dout is the ideal selected 4:1-mux value; final 4:1 mux propagation delay is omitted. The illustrative 0.25-UI delays apply only to the 8:4 mux and the latches.

foot.text: Time in UI. 8:4 mux / latch delay = 0.25 UI (illustrative); 4:1 output ideal.
